summary: Runner credential propagation lag after secret rotation blocks nightly release gate
description:
Issue summary:
During the automated scheduled secrets rotation (2026-03-10 02:00 UTC), a subset of ephemeral CI runners in the prod/us-west fleet did not receive newly-wrapped service credentials for the release-deployer role. As a result the nightly release pipeline entered the 'gate' step and remained blocked with runner jobs pending for ~90 minutes, delaying the cutover.

Impact:
- Nightly release pipeline stalled for customer-facing build at 02:15-03:45 UTC (approx 1.5hr delay).
- ~12 pipeline jobs moved into pending state waiting for runner tokens and failed with 401/403 from internal artifact registry.
- No customer-facing production outages, but release cadence and dependent downstream migrations were delayed.

Environment:
- prod cluster: k8s-prod-uswest (region us-west-2)
- CI orchestrator: internal-build (v3.4.1)
- Runner image: rwd-runner:v2026-02-28
- Vault: transit rewraps initiated against mount kv-v2/ci-secrets

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 02:00 UTC - automated rotation job kicked off (jenkins job ID 4721) to rewrap deployer service-account keys and rotate vault transit encryption keys.
2) Rotation job completed (logs show success), new wrapped payloads pushed to kv-v2/ci-secrets.
3) CI-config controller attempted to inject refreshed secrets to ephemeral runner pods; controller logs show exponential retry and backoff for a subset of runner pods.
4) Runners that failed to update continued presenting old tokens; artifact registry and registry-proxy returned 403.
5) Nightly release gate jobs attempted to schedule on runners; scheduler marked them pending awaiting healthy runners.

Logs / evidence:
- Vault audit events: vault-audit-prod.log (entries around 2026-03-10T02:00:xxZ) show successful rewrap but also several DECRYPT errors for pods with stale KMS envelope ids.
- Runner controller: controller-prod.log excerpts show "secret fetch timeout" and then "ciphertext key id mismatch" for 12 runner pods.
- Scheduler metrics: build-scheduler dashboard spike in pending jobs (chart id scheduler/pendings-2026-03-10).
- Artifact proxy returned 403 with body: "service-account-token-expired" for affected pods.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Support temporarily pinned nightly pipeline to use dedicated standby runners (dedicated pool: rdw-dedicated-standby) at 03:30 UTC to allow release to proceed.
- Team re-ran a targeted spawn of new ephemeral runners with a forced secret refresh; 8 of 12 affected pods successfully joined after re-spawn.

Current state (at updated_at):
- Release resumed and completed at 03:45 UTC using fallback path.
- 4 runner pods remain in a failed state and will be drained and re-created on next maintenance window.

Requested outcome:
- Identify root cause of propagation lag and implement fix to ensure runners pick up rotated secrets within SLO for future rotations.
- Add health-checking and faster eviction path for runners that do not accept new credentials within 5 minutes after rotation.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KMS re-encryption window produced new envelope IDs that older runner bootstrap logic cannot resolve - evidenced by 'ciphertext key id mismatch' in controller logs.

Checked Vault and KMS: rotation job logged successful rewraps; however audit trail shows intermittent 503s to KMS endpoint at 2026-03-10T01:59:12Z that coincide with a short region-wide control-plane spike (see cloud-provider status event id cp-33012).

Controller behavior: secret-injector has a 30s fetch timeout and exponential backoff; when KMS returned transient 503s earlier, some pods cached the old ciphertext and never refreshed due to backoff ceiling bug (observed backoff linger > 15 minutes).
Corroborating evidence: 8 pods recovered after forced re-spawn; 4 pods had stuck init containers that never hit the refresh code path due to a race between sidecar init and mount readiness.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10T03:05Z: Noted that nightly release is blocked and customers on staging reported no issue. Escalating to SRE and Release Eng.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) - 2026-03-10T03:18Z: Investigating vault audit logs and runner controller. Found repeated KMS 503s at rotation time. Spawning standby runners to allow release to continue; pinning pipeline to dedicated pool.
Priya Nair (Release Eng) - 2026-03-10T04:00Z: Release resumed using fallback; will require a postmortem and mitigation to avoid future delays. Adding task to change rotation schedule if needed.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) - 2026-03-11T10:12Z: Deployed hotfix to secret-injector backoff logic (github.com/redwood-inference/runners/commit/2f9c8b5). New config reduces max backoff to 60s and retries aggressively for initial 3 attempts.
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-12T09:30Z: Noted that ops confirmed no further incidents after hotfix; keeping ticket open for follow-up tasks.
root_cause: Transient KMS gateway 503s during the key rewrap window combined with a bug in the secret-injector's backoff policy caused a subset of ephemeral runners to retain stale wrapped credentials. The backoff ceiling prevented timely retries, and an init-container race prevented fallbacks for some pods.
resolution: Hotfix merged to secret-injector to cap backoff and force an early eviction on failed initial fetches (commit 2f9c8b5). Added a maintenance job to drain and re-create any runner pods that do not report successful secret refresh within 5 minutes post-rotation. Nightly rotation schedule under review to avoid KMS maintenance windows.
suggested_followups: Add automated canary rotation test that validates a small subset of runners pick up new secrets within 2 minutes post-rotate
Instrument secret-injector metrics to emit 'secret_refresh_latency' and alert if > 2m for > 5% of fleet
Coordinate with cloud-provider to avoid key rewraps during known control-plane instability windows
Postmortem write-up and runbook update: include explicit steps for fallback to dedicated runner pool and steps to manually force refresh on stuck pods
